recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Repair or replace
recent_violations.inspector_comments: THIS 3 STORY BUILDING HAS NUMEROUS EXTERIOR DOORS IN A STATE OF SEVERE DISREPAIR. THIS NARRATIVE WILL REFER TO EACH AND EVERY EXTERIOR FRONT ENTRY DOOR AT GRADE; EACH AND EVERY BALCONY ACCESS DOOR AND ANY OF THE APARTMENT FRONT DOORS IN DISREPAIR (SOME OF THE  APARTMENT ENTRANCE DOORS ARE OPERABLE). ALL OF THE AFFECTED DOORS SHARE THE FOLLOWING DEFECTS; DAMAGED OR MISSING LOCK HARDWARE, DAMAGED OR MISSING SELF-CLOSING DEVICES, DAMAGED HINGES, DAMAGED DOOR FRAMES, DOORS NOT CLOSING FLUSH WITH DOOR FRAME AND DOORS NOT LOCKING. THE POOR CONDITION OF THE FRONT EXTERIOR BUILDING ENTRANCE DOORS, AS WELL AS BALCONY ACCESS DOORS, HAS RENDERED THIS ENTIRE BUILDING AS UNSECURE. THERE IS ABSOLUTELY NO BASIC BUILDING SECURITY AS A RESULT OF THE EXTERIOR DOORS(S) CONDITION. ALSO, MOST OF THE STORM / SCREEN DOORS ARE MISSING / INOPERABLE. THIS CONDITION IS TO BE CONSIDERED DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS. ALL AFFECTED DOORS ARE TO BE REPLACED WITH NEW DOOR & FRAME SETS. PERMIT REQUIRED.SECTION 14X-3-303.13, 14X-3-303.17 AND 14X-12-1202.4.3.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install and maintain approved smoke detectors. (13-196-100 thru 13-196-160) Install a smoke detector in every dwelling unit. Install one on any living level with a habitable room or unenclosed heating plant, on the uppermost ceiling of enclosed porch stairwell, and within 15 feet of every sleeping room. Be sure the detector is at least 4 inches from the wall, 4 to 12 inches from the ceiling, and not above door or window.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.inspector_comments: AS PER SECTION 14A-4-401.1, IT'S UNLAWFUL TO CONSTRUCT, ALTER, REHABILITATE OR CHANGE THE OCCUPANCY WITHOUT FIRST OBTAINING A PERMIT. AT THE TIME OF INSPECTION, THE FOLLOWING-BUT NOT LIMITED TO, INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR ALTERATIONS WERE OBSERVED; THE ORIGINAL PORCH SYSTEM AT THE REAR WAS ENCLOSED AND ATTACHED TO THE REAR OF THE HOUSE. A NEW EXTERIOR STAIR SYSTEM WITH A HANDICAP RAMP WAS CONSTRUCTED AT THE REAR, 6FT SOLID WOOD FENCING WAS ERECTED AT THE REAR OF THE LOT ENCLOSING THE YARD AREA AND SEPARATING THE PARKING AREA. THE FIRST FLOOR HAD THE INTERIOR OF THE KITCHEN AREA ENLARGED BY REMOVING THE ORIGINAL EXTERIOR WALL AND ANNEXING THE ENCLOSED PORCH SYSTEM AS ADDITIONAL LIVING SPACE. THE STAIR SYSTEM TO THE ATTIC WAS MODIFIED TO ACCESS THE ATTIC SPACE AREA, WHEREAT 2 BEDROOMS AND A HALF BATHROOM WERE FORMED. THE BASEMENT AREA WAS TRANFORMED FROM INCIDENTAL STORAGE AND MECHANICAL AREA TO INCLUDE 2 BEDROOMS, A FULL BATHROOM, LAUNDRY AREA, LOUNGE AREA, FURNACE AND WATER HEATER MECHANICAL ROOM. A SUBSEQUENT PERMIT SEARCH DIDN'T IDENTIFY THE REQUIRED PERMIT FOR ALL LISTED ALTERATIONS THAT INCLUDES, ELECTRICAL, PLUMBING AND HVAC ALTERATIONS/ADDITIONS. DUE TO THE EXTENSIVE ALTERATIONS INSIDE AND OUT, A DETAILED ARCHITECTURAL PLAN AND RENOVATION PERMIT IS NOW REQUIRED TO LEGALIZE ALL WORK PERFORMED WITHOUT A PERMIT.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.
